critical_issues.description: Truncated assertion string: 'not found' in data['det' is incomplete and will cause a SyntaxError.

The regex pattern in test_app_js_contains_expected_api_endpoints does not account for escaped quotes in strings (e.g., "\/api\/v1\/health"), which could cause false negatives in real-world minified or transpiled JS.
test_app_js_contains_fetch_calls_with_expected_paths duplicates the exact logic and pattern of test_app_js_contains_expected_api_endpoints, violating DRY and test uniqueness principles.

The test for exports/functions is overly permissive and will pass for any JS file containing arbitrary variable declarations (e.g., 'const x = 1'), even if no meaningful API logic exists—does not verify actual /api/v1/health usage or function names.
Direct import of app from src.main may cause circular import or side effects during test setup; should use factory pattern or fixture to ensure clean app initialization.

Test assumes /api/v1/health returns exactly 'healthy' status, but API contract only specifies 'status' as string; should validate against contract more loosely (e.g., non-empty string) to avoid brittleness.

Test for /dashboard checks for specific static asset paths in HTML, which couples test to implementation details (file paths, build artifacts); should instead verify presence of required UI elements or use content-negotiation (e.g., check for expected text or structured data).

Test file name 'test_static_css_style.css.py' is misleading and non-standard; pytest expects test files to end in 'test_*.py' or '*_test.py', and this name suggests it's a CSS file, not a Python test.

The test 'test_css_file_contains_css_variables' incorrectly assumes CSS variables must be defined via ':root' or 'var()'; CSS variables can be defined in any selector (e.g., 'body { --primary: blue; }'), and 'var()' usage alone doesn't confirm variable *definition*.
test_health_endpoint mocks api_router unnecessarily and tests /health instead of the documented /api/v1/health endpoint, violating the API contract.
test_docs_endpoint_exists checks for /docs but does not verify the actual health endpoint (/api/v1/health) exists as per API contract.

Module-level mutation of app (app.include_router(router)) causes side effects during import, which violates test isolation and can cause unpredictable behavior when tests run in parallel or when the module is imported elsewhere.
Test functions directly use a global app instance instead of a fixture, making tests non-isolated and dependent on import order/state.

Missing import for 'Path' from 'pathlib' is already present, but the code uses 'Path(__file__)' without ensuring 'Path' is imported — however, it *is* imported correctly. This is not an issue. The real critical issue is the missing /api/v1/health endpoint required by the API contract.
Missing required /api/v1/health endpoint as specified in API contracts.

Missing import for HTTPException status_code validation; FastAPI requires explicit status_code parameter in HTTPException for proper error responses, but more critically, the code lacks proper exception handling for database operations that could leak connections.
Database connection not closed in case of exception (cursor.execute or fetchall may fail before conn.close()), risking connection leaks.
Database connection not closed in case of exception during INSERT operation, risking connection leaks.
Database connection not closed in case of exception during SELECT operation in get_inundation_map(), risking connection leaks.
Missing closing parenthesis in HTTPException call (incomplete code), causing syntax error.
Missing health check endpoint '/api/v1/health' as required by API contracts.
Incomplete CSS rule: '.text-center {' is missing closing brace and declaration block, causing cascade failure for subsequent rules.
File begins with invalid syntax: triple-quoted string literal (Python-style) instead of valid JavaScript. This will cause immediate parse failure in all browsers.

DOM object contains over 70 properties, many of which appear to be redundant or misnamed (e.g., evacuationMapProgressLoadStartAbortErrorHandlerTimeoutAbortErrorHandlerTimeoutHandler), indicating likely copy-paste error or incomplete refactoring. This bloats memory and increases maintenance risk.
DOM object is declared but never initialized (no document.querySelector calls), so all DOM references will be null, causing runtime errors when used.
API_BASE is hardcoded as '/api/v1', but no code is present to actually make API calls (e.g., fetch) or handle the health endpoint response as required by the dashboard.

moderate_issues.description: Module docstring is minimal; should include purpose, scope, and usage notes for test fixtures.
mock_db fixture returns a generic MagicMock without any realistic interface simulation; could mask missing method calls or incorrect usage in tests.
mock_redis fixture returns a generic MagicMock without simulating Redis client behavior (e.g., get/set/pipeline); may lead to false-positive tests.
The router may be a FastAPI instance already; the conditional wrapping it in another app is unnecessary and could mask issues if router is not a standard FastAPI instance.
Test assumes get_items returns exactly one item; lacks test for empty list case.
create_item test does not validate that the function is called with correct parameters beyond the payload (e.g., no validation of user context, db session, etc., if applicable).
Validation error test uses empty payload but does not verify the exact validation error structure beyond status code; should assert on error detail (e.g., 'field required' for 'name').
get_item_by_id side_effect uses ValueError, but FastAPI typically converts exceptions to HTTPException; ensure the router properly handles ValueError or use HTTPException in tests for accuracy.

The health endpoint test assumes a fixed response structure, but the API contract specifies only 'status' as a string; it should validate the response schema more robustly (e.g., using Pydantic model parsing or at least checking the key exists and is a string).

The static files test checks for a specific string in the HTML body ('real-time-urban-flood-inundation-mapping'), which is brittle and may change independently of functionality; better to verify structural elements (e.g., presence of <html>, <head>, <body>) or use a more stable identifier.
The fixture app_js_path hardcodes the path; should use configurable or environment-aware path to support different environments (e.g., Docker, CI).
Regex pattern does not handle template literals (e.g., fetch(`/api/v1/health`) or fetch(`${baseURL}/health`), limiting robustness.
The test does not verify that the function(s) defined actually make the required API call; presence of 'export' or 'function' is insufficient to confirm contract compliance.
Test for /static/index.html lacks validation of response content type or body structure; should assert Content-Type header and/or verify HTML structure to ensure correct serving.
Missing validation of response headers (e.g., Content-Type for HTML responses); production tests should verify headers match expected values.

The test 'test_css_file_contains_expected_design_system_properties' checks for substring presence (e.g., 'color') which may yield false positives (e.g., 'color' in a comment or string literal); should use regex or more precise parsing to detect actual property declarations.
Basic brace/parentheses balancing checks are insufficient for robust CSS syntax validation; they ignore nested structures, comments, and quoted strings where braces/parens may appear legitimately.

Fixture 'css_file_path' returns a relative path; in production test environments, working directory may vary—should use absolute path resolution (e.g., Path(__file__).parent.parent / 'static' / 'css' / 'style.css') for reliability.
test_app_includes_router inspects app.routes but does not verify the router was added via app.include_router() — could pass even if router was never attached.
test_health_endpoint uses patch on api_router which is irrelevant and may mask issues in app setup; health endpoint should be tested directly.
test_openapi_schema_exists does not verify the presence of the documented /api/v1/health endpoint in the OpenAPI schema, which is required for API contract validation.
Test client is instantiated inside each test function instead of using a fixture, leading to redundant setup and reduced maintainability.
Importing app from src.main and modifying it at module level may cause circular import issues or interfere with app initialization logic (e.g., startup events, middleware).
STATIC_DIR resolution may break in packaged/frozen applications (e.g., PyInstaller) because __file__ may not point to the expected location.

read_dashboard() returns raw HTML as JSON when index.html exists, but returns a dict with 'error' key when missing — inconsistent response types (should return 404 with error or consistent structure).
No error handling for file I/O (e.g., permission errors, disk issues) when reading index.html.

DEBUG flag derived directly from ENV without validation; could be bypassed if APP_ENV is set to arbitrary non-'development' string (e.g., 'production' vs 'staging' vs 'test') — should validate against known environments.
DATABASE_URL uses a default SQLite path that may be insecure or inappropriate for production; should validate URL scheme and raise if production environment uses SQLite.
REDIS_URL default points to localhost; in production this may cause connection failures or unintended local usage — should validate or require explicit value in non-dev environments.
ML_MODEL_PATH uses a hardcoded relative path fallback; should validate existence or provide clear error if not found in production.
No input validation for datetime fields in models; pydantic validates types but not timezone-awareness, which may cause issues with SQLite's naive datetime storage.
Using raw SQL with string interpolation in INSERT (though using parameterized query here, which is good), but no validation that timestamp is in UTC or consistent timezone handling.
No rate limiting or input size limits for POST /api/sensors, risking DoS via large payloads.
No pagination support for list endpoints (/api/sensors, /api/inundation), which may cause performance issues as data grows.
No authentication/authorization mechanisms, exposing sensitive flood data endpoints.
Missing database schema validation; no checks for table existence before queries.

Logger level is set to INFO after adding handler, but if the logger already exists and has a different level, this will override it unexpectedly. Better to set level before adding handler or use logging.getLogger(name) with explicit level configuration.

Using a mutable default check (if not logger.handlers) is safe here, but the pattern can be fragile in multi-threaded environments where multiple threads may simultaneously detect no handlers and add duplicates. Consider using logging.config.dictConfig or a more robust initialization pattern for production.
Color contrast between --color-primary (#1e6f8c) and --color-neutral-800 (#212529) may fall below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal text; verify with contrast checker.
Missing CSS custom property for --font-weight-* variables; inconsistent font weights may harm readability and accessibility.
Z-index scale lacks values for map layers (e.g., markers, popups), which are critical for the flood mapping dashboard.
Missing responsive typography scale (e.g., fluid font sizes using clamp() or media queries) for mobile-first design.

DOM object uses camelCase for property names but includes many overly granular map state variables (e.g., evacuationMapDragStartX, evacuationMapZoomCenterY) that suggest incomplete abstraction—should be encapsulated in a dedicated map controller class.

DOM object contains no references to widgets mentioned in design (e.g., status widget), and no initialization logic for status card, lastUpdated, or errorContainer—violating the frontend_pages requirement.
No error handling, loading states, or retry logic for API calls—required for graceful degradation per design checklist.
No event listener cleanup (e.g., removeEventListener) for handlers like evacuationMapWheelHandler, risking memory leaks on navigation or re-renders.

suggestions: Consider using `unittest.mock.create_autospec` or defining custom mock classes to better reflect real database/Redis interfaces.
Add type hints to fixture return types (e.g., `-> MagicMock`) for improved IDE and type checker support.
Document expected methods/attributes on mock objects in fixture docstrings to guide test writers.
If actual database or Redis interactions are tested elsewhere, consider adding integration tests with real or containerized services.
Add `autouse=True` or explicit usage notes if these fixtures are intended to be used across many test modules.
Add tests for missing endpoints (e.g., 404 on unknown paths) to improve coverage.
Include tests for other documented endpoints (e.g., PUT/DELETE if applicable) to ensure full contract coverage.
Use pytest.raises() for exception-based tests instead of side_effect where appropriate for clarity.
Add type hints to test functions for better IDE support and documentation.
Consider using @pytest.fixture for mock setup to reduce duplication across tests.
Verify that the router's error handlers convert ValueError to 404 as expected; if not, update router or adjust test expectations.
Add test for malformed JSON in POST requests to ensure robustness.
Ensure all tests use consistent naming and structure (e.g., snake_case for test names).
Add type hints to test functions (e.g., `def test_main_app_exists() -> None:`) for consistency and IDE support.
Consider using `@pytest.fixture` for the `TestClient(app)` to avoid repeated instantiation and improve test isolation.
Add tests for error cases (e.g., unexpected server errors, malformed responses) to ensure robustness.
Use `response.raise_for_status()` before asserting JSON to catch HTTP errors early.
Verify that the static file path `/` is intentional — if the app serves a SPA or index at `/`, consider adding a dedicated `/index.html` route or explicit static file mount test.
Merge duplicate tests (test_app_js_contains_expected_api_endpoints and test_app_js_contains_fetch_calls_with_expected_paths) into a single, more robust test.
Add a test to verify that the response schema is handled (e.g., check for .json() or .then() chains after fetch calls to /api/v1/health).
Use pytest's tmp_path fixture to generate a temporary app.js for testing, avoiding reliance on static file existence.
Consider using a JS parser (e.g., esprima or acorn via subprocess) instead of regex for more reliable parsing of JS code.
Add a test to ensure the app.js file is not minified (or handle minified code explicitly) to improve test readability and maintainability.
Add type hints to function signatures and fixture return types for better IDE and mypy support.
Include a timeout or error handling for read_text() in case of large files or I/O issues.
Use pytest fixtures to manage TestClient lifecycle and app state for better isolation and reusability.
Add type hints to test functions and assertions for improved IDE support and documentation.
Consider using pydantic models to validate JSON response schemas against the API contracts.
Add tests for error cases (e.g., 404, 500) to ensure robustness.
Replace hardcoded static asset path checks with assertions on rendered HTML elements or structured data (e.g., JSON-LD, microdata) to decouple from build pipeline details.
Rename test file to 'test_static_css_style.py' to follow pytest naming conventions.
Replace substring-based CSS checks with a proper CSS parser (e.g., `cssutils`) for robust validation.
Add type hints to fixture and test functions for better IDE and static analysis support.
Consider adding a test to verify CSS file is readable and not corrupted (e.g., UTF-8 decoding success).
Document the expected CSS file location relative to project root in README or CI config to avoid path ambiguity.
Add pytest markers (e.g., @pytest.mark.css) to allow selective test execution.
Consider adding a test for CSS file size upper bound (e.g., < 1MB) to catch accidental binary inclusion.
Add a test for the actual /api/v1/health endpoint with correct path and response schema.
Remove unnecessary mocking in test_health_endpoint; test the real endpoint behavior.
Verify that app.include_router(api_router) is called during app initialization (e.g., via inspection or integration test).
Update test_openapi_schema_exists to assert the presence and correctness of the /api/v1/health endpoint in the OpenAPI schema.
Ensure src/main.py exports only intended public symbols and avoids module-level try/except ImportError.
Add type hints to all test functions and fixtures for better IDE and mypy support.
Use a pytest fixture (e.g., @pytest.fixture) to create and configure a fresh app instance per test or per test session.
Replace module-level app mutation with app factory pattern or fixture-based setup to ensure test isolation.
Consider using pytest’s built-in TestClient fixture if available (e.g., via pytest-asyncio or custom fixture) to avoid manual TestClient instantiation.
Add type hints to test functions and payloads for better IDE support and documentation.
Add parametrized tests for different valid/invalid payloads to improve coverage.
Verify that the API endpoint paths in tests match exactly those defined in the router (e.g., check for trailing slashes or versioning mismatches).
Add the required /api/v1/health endpoint returning {"status": "healthy"}.
Use FastAPI's FileResponse or return HTMLResponse for static HTML to avoid wrapping in JSON.
Add type hints to all endpoints (e.g., -> dict, -> HTMLResponse).
Add HTTPException for error cases (e.g., 404 when dashboard missing).
Consider using os.environ or config file for static directory path to improve deployability.
Add logging for dashboard access failures.
Ensure static directory exists at startup and log a warning if not.
Add type hints for all configuration variables (e.g., using typing.Optional, Literal for ENV).
Implement environment validation (e.g., ensure APP_ENV is one of ['development', 'staging', 'production']).
Add validation for DATABASE_URL to ensure it's not SQLite in production.
Add validation for ML_MODEL_PATH to check file existence before use.
Consider using pydantic or dynaconf for structured config validation and type coercion.
Add logging or warnings when defaults are used instead of environment variables.
Add docstrings explaining expected format for each environment variable.
Use contextlib.closing or try/finally to ensure database connections are always closed.
Add health check endpoint as specified in API contracts.
Implement proper logging instead of returning raw exception strings in HTTPException details.
Add input sanitization for string fields (e.g., strip whitespace, validate against allowlists).
Consider using an async database driver (e.g., asyncpg) for better scalability.
Add database migrations or schema initialization to ensure tables exist before queries.
Implement request validation middleware to catch malformed inputs early.
Add CORS middleware if this API serves frontend from different origin.
Use Pydantic's BaseModel.model_validate() for explicit validation in handlers.
Add database connection pooling for production scalability.
Consider allowing configuration of log level and formatter via parameters for flexibility.
Add support for environment variable overrides (e.g., LOG_LEVEL) to enable runtime tuning without code changes.
Use logging.basicConfig() or a dedicated configuration function for more predictable behavior in complex applications.
Add type hints for handler and formatter to improve IDE support and static analysis.
Consider adding a null handler fallback for library modules to prevent 'No handler found' warnings.
Add media query support for responsive spacing (e.g., --spacing-md-sm, --spacing-md-md) using clamp() or @media.
Include --font-weight-* variables (e.g., --font-weight-light, --font-weight-bold) for semantic typography.
Add focus-visible polyfill fallback or use :focus-visible instead of :focus for better keyboard navigation.
Define --color-on-* variables (e.g., --color-on-primary, --color-on-danger) to ensure text contrast on colored backgrounds.
Add a dark mode theme with --color-scheme: dark; and corresponding variable overrides.
Include --aspect-ratio-* variables for consistent media container sizing (e.g., maps, charts).
Add --transition-easing-* variables (e.g., ease-in-out, cubic-bezier) for more precise animation control.
Ensure all interactive elements have explicit :hover and :active states with visual feedback.
Replace the invalid triple-quoted string with a proper JSDoc comment block using /** ... */.
Refactor DOM references into a proper initialization function using document.querySelectorAll and store in a single DOM object.
Implement the health check API call using fetch with async/await and error handling.
Add real status display logic (e.g., update statusCard text based on health response).
Remove redundant/unused map state variables and encapsulate map interaction logic in a separate module.
Add accessibility attributes (aria-live, role, tabindex) to status and loading elements.
Define and use CSS custom properties (e.g., --color-status-ok, --font-main) in style.css to support the required color palette and typography.
Add a proper entry point (e.g., document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init)) to ensure DOM readiness before manipulation.
